Provide technical and project management support to litigation teams throughout the eDiscovery lifecycle.
Manage Relativity, Brainspace, and other litigation technology platforms, including database setup, advanced searches, review workflows, and productions.
Advise case teams on technology solutions, data management strategies, and eDiscovery best practices.
Develop and implement TAR, CAL, and advanced analytics workflows to support document review, prioritization, privilege identification, and quality control.

Hands-on experience with eDiscovery platforms such as Relativity, DISCO, and Recommind, including database administration, advanced searching, and review workflow development.

Experience managing multiple technical projects, coordinating resources, and meeting competing deadlines.

Strong communication, analytical, troubleshooting, and organizational skills.

Experience delivering technical training and communicating complex concepts to legal professionals.
Flexibility to work overtime as project demands require.

Bachelor's degree preferred; an associate's degree with equivalent professional experience will be considered.
Relativity Certified Administrator (RCA), Brainspace Analyst, and PMP certifications preferred.

jobs.title: Project Manager - Government
jobs.description:
The Project Manager independently manages technology projects or serves as a Project Manager within a broader program with guidance available from more experienced coworkers. Projects are typically low to medium in complexity and risk and may involve mainstream, legacy, or select emerging technologies, a defined solution area, and third-party providers. The Project Manager owns day-to-day project delivery from initiation through closure and works with sales, consultants, clients, subcontractors, and cross-functional delivery teams. The role is accountable for managing project scope, schedule, budget, contractual deliverables, risks, issues, quality, and stakeholder expectations within established parameters. The Project Manager acts as a project advocate by driving results, supporting timely decisions, and building effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.

What You Will Do

Project Management: Independently manages low- to medium-complexity projects using CDW-G’s established delivery methodology and standard project management templates. Adapts project artifacts as needed within established practices to meet the needs of the engagement.
Ensures the client’s documented business, technical, contractual, and operational requirements are understood and addressed throughout project delivery.
Manages Stakeholders: Identifies project stakeholders, confirms success criteria and expectations, and involves the appropriate stakeholders in project decisions. Builds effective relationships and remains focused on meeting stakeholder expectations.
Accountable for project financial performance within the approved budget. Monitors, interprets, and communicates project budget, actuals, forecast, and estimate-at-completion information. Escalates significant variances and supports corrective actions.
Ensures project time, expenses, invoices, and financial records are accurately tracked, reviewed, and approved in a timely manner.
Validates initial project scope, assumptions, estimates, deliverables, and acceptance criteria. Manages the change-control process, assesses impacts to scope, schedule, cost, resources, and risk, and determines whether a Change Order or new Statement of Work may be required.
Ensures all items defined in the CDW Statement of Work are delivered and performs quality assurance throughout the project life cycle.
Identifies, analyzes, documents, and manages project risks, issues, assumptions, constraints, and dependencies. Develops mitigation actions, assigns ownership, tracks progress, and escalates items when appropriate.
Develops, maintains, adjusts, and communicates project schedules, tasks, milestones, and dependencies in collaboration with the project team, client, subcontractors, and third-party providers.
Supports resource planning by identifying resource needs, monitoring assignments and billable schedules, and escalating resource or scheduling constraints that could affect delivery.
Manages equipment, software, licensing, outside services procurement, and delivery schedules applicable to the project.
Responsible for meeting contractual performance requirements, deliverables, acceptance criteria, milestones, and due dates within the assigned project.
Ensures compliance with applicable corporate, client, and government policies and requirements.
Applies an understanding of government contract vehicles, Blanket Purchase Agreements, purchasing vehicles, and acquisition requirements to assigned project execution, reporting, invoicing, changes, and completion.
Supports projects delivered under contract types that may include Firm Fixed Price, Time and Materials, Cost Plus, and As-a-Service arrangements.
Leadership: Takes accountability for assigned project outcomes and demonstrates fiscal responsibility to the client, the project, and CDW-G. Establishes clear task ownership and follows up on assigned responsibilities.
Builds trust and credibility through reliable delivery, sound judgment, business awareness, and professional stakeholder relationships.
Contributes to the continuous improvement of project management standards, templates, tools, best practices, and shared knowledge resources.
Communication: Determines and maintains the appropriate project documentation, including schedules, status reports, budget information, quality plans, risk and issue logs, decision records, action items, and closure documentation.
Communicates clear, concise, audience-appropriate project updates to clients, sales, delivery teams, and other stakeholders. Escalates decisions and issues requiring leadership support.
Leads effective in-person and virtual project meetings. Maintains focus, documents outcomes, assigns action items, and distributes timely follow-up communications.
Adapts communication style, content, and medium to the audience and project environment. Communicates difficult or complex project information clearly and professionally.
Negotiation: Gathers relevant information and seeks input from Sales or Services leadership when needed. Negotiates project changes involving cost, scope, schedule, effort, or resource commitments within assigned authority.
Problem Solving and Decision Making: Works with team members to gather information, assess potential project impacts, identify response options, document mitigation steps, and communicate decisions to the team and client.
Documents project outcomes and lessons learned and shares them appropriately with colleagues.

What We Expect Of You

Bachelor’s degree in business, computer science, information technology, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Three years of experience delivering technology through structured Project Management methodologies such as waterfall or agile.
Two or more years of experience leading significant projects within a single technology solution area.
Demonstrated ability to manage low- to medium-complexity technology projects and take accountability for assigned project outcomes.
Experience supporting projects for enterprise, strategic, or government customers.
Ability to manage project budgets, schedules, scope, risks, issues, changes, and contractual deliverables within established parameters.
Working knowledge of one or more formal project management methodologies and proficiency with Microsoft Project, Microsoft Office, and related project management tools.
Ability to apply business acumen, sound judgment, perseverance, and communication skills to build credibility with project stakeholders.
Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and facilitation skills, including the ability to communicate project information to business and technical stakeholders.
Ability to participate productively in virtual teams and contribute to improvements in project management processes
Applies discretion when handling sensitive or confidential information.
Ability to balance multiple priorities, adapt to changing business needs, and meet deadlines.
Ability to work weekends or outside standard business hours when necessary to meet client needs.
Ability and willingness to travel up to 25% or as needed to other CDW locations, meetings, and client sites.
PMP certification required, is a plus.
Active DoD Secret clearance strongly preferred, is a plus.
Familiarity with government contracts, acquisition processes, and government programs, is a plus.
Familiarity with FISMA and FedRAMP requirements, is a plus.
Business and technical acumen related to Federal initiatives, is a plus.
Experience supporting business value or impact analysis, is a plus.

Pay range: $85,000 - $126,200 depending on experience and skill set

Annual bonus target of 10% subject to terms and conditions of plan

Benefits overview: https://cdw.benefit-info.com/

Salary ranges may be subject to geographic differentials

Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.

So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff. Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place. Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.

Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. Own the end-to-end quality assurance framework application to cryptocurrency and sanctions compliance decisions

Strong knowledge of compliance regulations, risks, and typologies, paired with an analytical, metrics-driven approach to building substantiated solutions
Excellent written and verbal communication skills and the organizational skills to manage competing priorities in an agile, fast-paced environment

jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Partner Ecosystem
jobs.description:
Why Socure?

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.

About The Role

Socure’s Partner Ecosystem brings third-party data and decisioning partners into RiskOS. Every partner we onboard has to be integrated cleanly, operated reliably, implemented correctly in customer environments, and understood well enough that our Solutions and Sales teams can put it to work. This role owns the technical side of all of it.

You will be the technical point of accountability for the RiskOS partner ecosystem. You will align with partners on an integration approach. Solutions teams come to you when an implementation doesn't behave. You will define scope, requirements, and priority for the Partner Integration engineering pod. Internal teams come to you to understand what a partner product actually does and when to use it.

This is not just a coordination or ticket-writing role. You will personally run partner API discovery, write the specs the pod builds from, sit in the middle of live troubleshooting, and own the documentation the rest of the company depends on. You will drive the partner engineering pod's roadmap and execution without managing the engineers directly — technical credibility, clarity, and relationships are how the work gets done here.

It is also a role that will grow. As our partner marketplace takes shape, you will be the technical driver behind it: defining what it takes for a partner product to be integrated and consumed at scale.

What You'll Do

Own partner integrations end to end

Own the program for every new integration: discovery, technical scope, specs, sequencing, and launch readiness — and the pod's roadmap, priorities, and capacity tradeoffs that deliver it.
Establish reusable integration patterns — authentication, data mapping, error handling, retries, fallbacks — so each new partner integration is faster than the last.
Work with Product and Legal/GRC so contractual and compliance constraints shape the design up front rather than surface as rework.

Be the technical counterpart to our partners

Serve as the primary technical contact for partner engineering and solutions teams, from API discovery through release and deprecation cycles.
Evaluate partner APIs, data models, SLAs, and support posture to identify the optimal integration path — and push back where their proposed pattern creates fragility, latency, cost, or compliance risk.
Define what "integration-ready" means for the marketplace — technical requirements, certification, acceptance criteria — and eventually hold that bar with partners who build into our platform themselves.

Make partner products succeed in customer environments

Work with pre-sales Solutions to help them understand partner products: what they do, what they require, what they cost, and what they can't do.
Work with post-sales Solutions and Implementation to ensure correct configuration across sandbox and production, and flag workflow designs that will produce poor decisioning outcomes.
Build the enablement material that lets Solutions teams handle routine cases independently.
Own triage and resolution for integration escalations, define monitoring requirements for integration health, and run a recurring audit cadence that produces remediation rather than a list of known issues.

Own documentation and product expertise — and scale it with AI

Own the technical documentation library: integration specs, API references, configuration guides, and troubleshooting runbooks. Treat documentation drift as a defect.
Use AI aggressively to draft specs and documentation — with the judgment to catch hallucinated behavior and verify against source API docs — and build repeatable AI patterns so throughput isn't bound by your calendar.
Develop working expertise in every partner product and act as the internal explainer for Sales, Solutions, Product, and Support.

What You Bring

5+ years in technical program management, technical product management, solutions architecture, solutions engineering, or integration engineering, including direct ownership of external-facing technical work.
Demonstrated ability to drive engineering execution without direct authority. You have owned a team's roadmap and delivery as an individual contributor and made it work through influence and credibility.
Deep, practical fluency with REST APIs, authentication patterns, webhooks, data mapping and normalization, and the failure modes of third-party dependencies. You can read an API doc set and immediately identify what will break in production.
Strong debugging instincts across distributed systems. You are comfortable in logs, traces, and payloads, and can isolate whether a problem is ours, the partner's, or a configuration issue.
Proven ability to work directly with external technical teams — holding a firm technical position, saying no well, and keeping the relationship intact.
Genuine people skills. This role runs on relationships: with partners, with engineers you don't manage, with Solutions teams under customer pressure, and with leadership. Technical strength alone will not carry it.
Exceptional written communication. The specs and documentation you produce are what other teams depend on; writing is a core competency here, not a nice-to-have.
Hands-on experience using AI tools in your actual workflow, with the discipline to verify output rather than trust it. You should be able to describe patterns you've built that made recurring work faster for more people than just yourself.
Comfort moving between a partner architecture discussion, a customer implementation escalation, and an internal enablement session in the same day.

Preferred Qualifications

Background in identity, fraud, risk, KYC/KYB, credit, or adjacent data-provider ecosystems.
Experience integrating and operating many third-party data vendors at scale, including managing vendor API versioning and deprecation.
Experience building or scaling a partner marketplace, app store, developer platform, or partner certification program.
Familiarity with decisioning or workflow orchestration platforms and how data products are composed within them.
Experience working alongside pre-sales and post-sales organizations in B2B enterprise SaaS.
Exposure to the compliance and contractual dimensions of third-party data use: data rights, permissible purpose, retention, and audit requirements.
Prior hands-on engineering background, even if you've since moved into solutions, program, or product work.

Socure is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity in all its forms within our company. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

If you need an accommodation during any stage of the application or hiring process—including interview or onboarding support—please reach out to your Socure recruiting partner directly.

jobs.title: Global Security Manager
jobs.description:
We are an applied AI lab building end-to-end software agents.

We're the makers of Devin, the first AI software engineer.

Our team is extremely talent-dense. Among our founding team, we have world-class competitive programmers, former founders, and leaders from companies at the cutting edge of AI including Scale AI, Palantir, Cursor, Waymo, Tesla, Lunchclub, Modal, Google DeepMind, and Nuro.

Building Devin is just the first step—our hardest challenges still lie ahead. If you’re excited to solve some of the world’s biggest problems and build AI that can reason on real-world tasks, apply to join us.

Role Mission

Cognition is growing fast, with teams in San Francisco, New York, London, Berlin, Tokyo, Singapore, Sydney and other cities, and customers that include some of the largest and most security-conscious institutions in the world, including the U.S. government. As a frontier AI company, our people, our offices and the systems we build are attractive targets for nation-state actors, criminals and activists.

The Global Security Manager builds and runs the program that protects Cognition's people, facilities, travel and events worldwide, and the physical and personnel security that supports our Federal division. This is a hands-on, high-trust role: you will set strategy and policy, run day-to-day security operations through a small team and trusted vendors, and be the decision-maker when something goes wrong. You will report to the Chief Security Officer and work closely with Threat Intel & Investigations, Corporate Security, IT, Workplace, People, Legal and the Federal team.

What You'll Accomplish

Risk & Threat Assessment: Monitor geopolitical, environmental, physical and cyber threats globally. Run threat and vulnerability assessments for offices, offsites, events and executive travel destinations, and partner with Threat Intel & Investigations on threats directed at our employees and leadership.
Policy & Strategy Development: Create and enforce security policies, standard operating procedures, emergency response plans and compliance standards worldwide, with a physical security strategy that scales as we open new offices and markets.
Crisis Management & Incident Response: Lead responses to safety threats, travel emergencies and critical incidents, from workplace violence to natural disasters. Own incident command, the mass notification system, and business continuity planning with Legal, People, Workplace and IT, and run post-incident reviews that turn every event into lasting improvements.
Physical Security Operations & Technology: Own access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection and visitor management across our offices. Set security standards for new office build-outs, and integrate physical access with our identity systems alongside Corporate Security and IT.
Team & Vendor Oversight: Manage security personnel, the security operations center (GSOC), and external guard, executive protection and technology vendors. Set performance metrics, manage contracts and budget, and hold partners to a high bar.
Travel & Executive Protection: Oversee global travel risk programs, tracking tools, pre-trip briefings and high-risk journey management. Run the executive protection program for our CEO and leadership team, including advance work, residential security assessments and event security.
Counterintelligence: Build Cognition's counterintelligence program to identify and counter efforts by foreign intelligence services and competitors to gain access to our people, technology and customers, including targeted recruitment, social engineering and elicitation. Provide regular counterintelligence briefings to executives and staff, especially before foreign travel, and partner with Threat Intelligence, the Facility Security Officer and government counterparts on suspected incidents.
Federal Division Security: Interface with our Facility Security Officer, who owns cleared facilities and personnel security, to provide appropriate protections in support of our FedRAMP, ITAR and IL5+ operations, including physical access controls, visitor and foreign-national controls, and insider risk programs.
External Partnerships: Build relationships with local and federal law enforcement, OSAC and peer security teams at other AI labs and technology companies to stay ahead of emerging risks and coordinate during incidents.
Automate with Devin: Use Devin and other AI agents to scale the program: threat and travel monitoring, alert triage, reporting and the operational work that usually requires a large headcount.

Exceptional Candidates Have Demonstrated

Program leadership: 8+ years in corporate or global security, including physical security, executive protection, GSOC operations and travel risk management, ideally at a fast-growing technology company. A background in law enforcement, the military or government is a plus.
Crisis judgment: Experience acting as the senior decision-maker during real incidents, staying calm under pressure, and communicating clearly to executives and employees.
Global, distributed operations: A track record of building or scaling security programs across multiple countries, including selecting and managing third-party vendors and owning a budget.
Industrial security: Familiarity with NISPOM (32 CFR Part 117) and ITAR, and experience working alongside Facility Security Officers to support cleared programs.
Discretion and writing: Strong written communication and the judgment to operate in a confidential, high-trust environment.
Builder mindset: Comfort working in a dynamic environment, moving quickly, and replacing manual processes with tooling and automation.
Background: Prior law enforcement, military, or intelligence experience is required.
Eligibility: US Citizen required, must be clearable to TS/SCI. Previous or current clearance is a plus. Ability to travel and to be available outside business hours during incidents. Certifications such as CPP or PSP are a plus.

Our Commitment

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities throughout the hiring process - please let us know if you need any. Cognition also considers applicants with criminal histories consistent with the SF Fair Chance Ordinance and similar local laws.

jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
Hyve Company Overview

Hyve Solutions transforms complex engineering challenges into production reality for technology innovators building AI, cloud, and connected infrastructure. As a US-based manufacturing partner, the company rapidly delivers fast, agile execution through dep technical partnerships and co-innovation, and supply chain clarity. Hyve’s integrated ODM, CM, and SI capabilities eliminate vendor complexity while accelerating time-to-market with single-partner accountability from design through scale. The company co-innovates with deep engineering expertise, treating customer success as its own while building tomorrow's digital infrastructure.

The Program Manager, Production Planning is responsible for driving production execution and planning strategies to support customer demand, on-time delivery performance, and operational excellence. This role leads cross-functional coordination across Supply Chain, Manufacturing Operations, Engineering, Warehouse, Sales, and Program Management teams to ensure production readiness, material availability, capacity planning, and schedule adherence. The Program Manager serves as a key stakeholder in production planning processes, inventory management, risk mitigation, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

Lead development and execution of the Master Production Schedule (MPS) to support customer demand and delivery commitments.
Forecast capacity and labor requirements based on production demand and business objectives.
Partner with Warehouse, Supply Chain, Engineering, Program Management, Sales, and Manufacturing Operations teams to ensure alignment of schedules, resources, and materials.
Oversee production material requirements from release through end-of-life and purge activities.
Manage WIP inventory performance and drive adherence to monthly inventory goals and operational metrics.
Identify schedule constraints, production bottlenecks, and capacity risks, and drive corrective actions to resolve issues.
Communicate program risks, schedule impacts, mitigation plans, and recovery strategies to leadership and stakeholders.
Lead cross-functional discussions to ensure production readiness and successful execution of customer requirements.
Develop, document, and improve standard work procedures related to production planning and scheduling.
Serve as a subject matter expert for production planning processes, systems, and tools.
Support training initiatives and mentoring of planning team members.
Drive process improvement activities focused on planning accuracy, inventory optimization, and operational efficiency.
Ensure compliance with company policies, customer requirements, and quality standards.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, Analytics, Engineering, or a related discipline; Industrial Engineering preferred. Equivalent experience may be considered.
5+ years of experience in manufacturing, production planning, supply chain, or operations management.
Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional projects or programs in a manufacturing environment.
Strong understanding of production planning, inventory management, capacity planning, and scheduling methodologies.
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and proficiency with ERP/MRP systems.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational capabilities.
Ability to prioritize multiple initiatives in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
Ability to influence stakeholders and drive decisions across functional teams.

Preferred Qualifications

APICS/CPIM, CSCP, PMP, or related certification.
Experience supporting high-volume manufacturing operations.
Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement methodologies.
Experience working with demand planning, S&OP, and production scheduling processes.

What’s in it for you

Benefit Insurance

Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
Health Savings Account (HSA)
Mental Health Care
401K with match

Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management.

We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation, more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We are looking for a driven Associate Solutions Engineering Program Manager to lead and mentor a team of Associate Solutions Engineers (ASEs) through their technical training journey. Manage program logistics, including scheduling, cohort management, managing travel, and tracking ASE progress in technical certifications and soft skill development.

Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities.

AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

Amazon Connect is an AI-powered customer experience solution that enables superior outcomes at a lower cost. Since its 2017 public launch, Amazon Connect has become an AI leader, transforming how organizations of all types interact with their customers.

As part of the AWS Connect, we have a vision to provide business applications, leveraging Amazon’s unique experience and expertise, that are used by millions of companies worldwide to manage day-to-day operations. We will accomplish this by accelerating our customers’ businesses through delivery of intuitive and differentiated technology solutions that solve enduring business challenges. We blend vision with curiosity and Amazon’s real-world experience to build opinionated, turnkey solutions. Where customers prefer to buy over build, we become their trusted partner with solutions that are no-brainers to buy and easy to use.

Amazon Connect is a highly disruptive cloud-based contact center that enables businesses to deliver engaging, dynamic, and personal customer service experiences. Amazon Connect is the result of the ten years of development that went into building the tools Amazon uses to provide its award winning customer service at massive scale and launching it as a publicly available AWS service. With Amazon Connect, you can create your own cloud-based contact center and be taking calls in minutes. Amazon Connect leverages the power of Artificial Intelligence and the large ecosystem of AWS services such as Amazon Lex, Amazon Polly, AWS Lambda, Amazon S3 and Amazon Kinesis to provide a truly frustration free, easy-to-use, extensible, and natural customer experience. With this technology, we are transforming an industry and the way customers interact with businesses and how agents service them.

We have a rapidly growing customer base and an exciting charter in front of us that includes solving highly complex engineering and algorithmic problems. We are looking for passionate and talented Technical Program Manager to join us to innovate on this new service that addresses customer needs to build modern contact centers in the cloud. The position represents a rare opportunity to be a part of a fast-growing business soon after launch, and help shape the technology and product as we grow. You will be playing a crucial role in developing the next generation contact center, and get the opportunity to design and deliver scaleable, resilient systems while maintaining a constant customer focus.

We are looking for a highly effective Principal Technical Program Manager that can lead a team to quickly design and deliver systems while maintaining a constant customer focus.

You will work with design, technical, and business leaders to set strategy and define the product. You will drive, track, and report the development effort to leadership and partners. You will be key leader responsible for delivering the distributed systems and analytics that will enable AWS to continue changing the software industry by delivering more capabilities to more customers.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

jobs.title: Project Manager, High-Voltage
jobs.description:
Clēnera is a tier-one developer and independent power producer located in Boise, Idaho, and is the U.S. subsidiary of Enlight Renewable Energy (Nasdaq: ENLT). We develop, finance, construct, own, and operate utility-scale solar and energy storage facilities throughout the United States. In its 2025 analysis of solar independent power producers, S&P Global ranked Clēnera as a top ten U.S. owner of planned installations in the next five years. Clēnera has over 1.9 GW of solar and 5.1 GWh of storage in operations or construction, and a development pipeline totaling 17.8 GW of solar and 51.1 GWh of storage across 23 states. Our company culture is at the core of everything we do, so you'll regularly find Caring, Committed, and Courageous individuals who value respectful, cross-functional collaboration with partners internally and externally. With our tremendous portfolio growth, we are increasing our headcount to meet the demands of the business. Are you ready to change the world with us?

ABOUT THE ROLE

The HV Project Manager represents the Owner (IPP) and leads all high-voltage (HV), protection & controls (P&C), SCADA/communications, testing, and commissioning activities for utility-scale solar and energy storage assets. You will own cost, schedule, scope, quality, and risk for the HV build and commissioning phases from pre-functional checks through energization, interconnection testing, COD, and turnover to Operations. The PM functions as the primary interface with utilities, Owner's Engineers, EPCs, testing/commissioning vendors, and internal stakeholders, ensuring systems are safe, compliant, utility-approved, and reliable for long-term operations.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own end-to-end HV and site wide commissioning project planning and control, establishing the WBS, baseline schedule, cash flow forecasts, procurement milestones, and resource plans.
Drive weekly schedule reviews, recovery planning, and critical path management with EPC and site leadership.
Lead HV and site wide commissioning cost management and forecasting, including monthly EAC/EVA updates, change order pricing validation, contingency management, pay application review/approval, and alignment of financial reporting with Project Controls and Finance.
Direct contract administration, ensuring scope clarity, deliverable compliance, and change management discipline; draft, negotiate, and recommend change orders and claims with clear schedule/cost impact analyses.
Coordinate cross-functional execution to ensure design completeness, permitting compliance, interconnection readiness, and QA/QC adherence.
Execute risk management throughout the lifecycle, maintaining the risk register, quantifying impacts, implementing mitigations, and escalating strategic risks to senior leadership with recommended actions.
Drive site safety culture and compliance, integrating HSSE requirements into schedules and work plans and ensuring EPC adherence to safety KPIs and incident reporting.
Manage external stakeholder relationships, including utilities, AHJs, landowners, third party inspectors, and lenders' engineers, ensuring timely reviews, approvals, and alignment on critical path items.
Produce executive ready reports and presentations, summarizing progress, risks, cash flow, and forecasted outcomes for internal leadership and, when applicable, board-level review.
Mentor and guide other members of the project team, delegating workstreams, providing technical direction, and building execution discipline across the project team.
Lead lessons learned and continuous improvement, capturing insights during closeout and feeding back process and contract improvement recommendations to Construction leadership.
Collaborate with individual departments, as well as cross-functionally with other departments within the organization.
Maintain organizational excellence in terms of project timelines and deliverables.
Demonstrates the Clēnera Core Values of Caring, Committed, and Courageous.
Other duties as assigned.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

Education: Bachelor's degree in construction management, electrical engineering, business, or related field experience.
Experience: Minimum of 5 years of experience in HV construction and commissioning project management.
Technology: Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, and an ability to learn company-specific software programs, tools, processes, and machines.
Skills/Attributes:
Strong understanding of schedule and cost controls, including critical path analysis, recovery planning, earned value, EAC forecasting, and cash flow management.
Strong EPC contract administration and negotiation skills, capable of structuring clear change orders, resolving claims, and driving accountability to contractual obligations.
Technical fluency in utility scale HV, construction, including civil works, MV/HV systems, SCADA, protection/controls, energy storage technology and commissioning sequences.
Adept at identifying systemic and emergent risks, quantifying impacts, and implementing mitigation actions that protect COD and budget objectives.
Ability to build trust and effectively coordinate with utilities, AHJs, inspectors, lenders' engineers, and EPC executives to clear critical path issues.
Clear, persuasive communication, producing concise, decision ready reporting for senior leadership and guiding the project team toward shared outcomes.
Demonstrated ability to lead highly effective teams, both internally and externally.
Self-motivated to work through complex problems and competing priorities, including a high level of detail and organization.
Effective verbal and written communication skills.

Travel: 25%

Clēnera pays 100% of employee and dependent premiums for a suite of medical, dental, and vision coverages.

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
jobs.description:
The Senior Project Manager (SPM) will play a critical leadership role in the delivery of a highly complex, ground-up ultra-luxury hotel, resort, and branded residential development on a remote island in the Caribbean. Qualified candidates must demonstrate extensive experience delivering large-scale, ground-up ultra-luxury hospitality projects, along with strong technical construction expertise and experience managing projects in remote or logistically challenging environments.

Candidates based in South Florida are strongly preferred due to the geographic proximity to CMD's current projects.

Under the general direction of the Project Director, the SPM will independently lead day-to-day project execution, including planning, design management, construction oversight, and coordination of multidisciplinary international teams. Acting as an extension of the client's team, the SPM will deliver CMD's Owner's Advisor Services throughout the project lifecycle, ensuring alignment with schedule, budget, quality, and client objectives while upholding CMD's core values of Stewardship, Collaboration, and Professionalism.

Duties & Responsibilities

Project Leadership and Client Relations

Assume primary responsibility for independently directing daytoday project execution, establishing projectspecific objectives, priorities, policies, and procedures, and ensuring accountability across all project disciplines.
Serve as a senior representative of the client in coordinating with ownership, internationally recognized architects and designers, engineering consultants, contractors, operators, and regulatory agencies. Lead highlevel project meetings, drive critical decisions, and provide executivelevel briefings on project milestones, financial performance, risks, and strategic recommendations.
Exercise independent judgment in anticipating and resolving complex project challenges, proactively identifying risks, evaluating technical and commercial implications, and implementing effective solutions while escalating major strategic matters to the Project Director.
Provide leadership and direction to multidisciplinary project teams, holding consultants and contractors accountable for performance, deliverables, and project objectives. Mentor junior project staff in technical coordination, design management, and project management methodologies and standards.

Pre-Development

Lead early planning efforts, including site analysis, feasibility studies, land planning, area programming, master planning, infrastructure assessments, and conceptual design, ensuring alignment with the client’s development objectives and ultraluxury hospitality expectations.
Direct technical due diligence of site conditions, infrastructure, environmental constraints, and development risks to inform project decisions.
Lead preliminary budgets, cost estimates, financial models, and master schedules; assess design feasibility and construction approaches.
Recommend project delivery, contracting, procurement, phasing, and bid packaging strategies suited to remote island logistics and available resources.
Coordinate entitlements, permitting, and regulatory approvals, identifying potential obstacles early.
Challenge early design solutions to align architectural vision with constructability, infrastructure, cost, and schedule.

Pre-Construction

Establish project communication, document control, roles, and accountability across international teams; lead design coordination and project control meetings.
Direct the multidisciplinary design process from concept through construction documentation, managing internationally recognized architects, engineers, interior designers, and specialty consultants to ensure coordinated, technically sound deliverables that meet project quality, schedule, and budget objectives.
Critically evaluate architectural and engineering designs for technical feasibility, interdisciplinary coordination, constructability, regulatory compliance, and alignment with the client's vision and luxury hospitality brand standards. Identify deficiencies, challenge proposed solutions, and direct appropriate corrective measures.
Evaluate detailed budgets, schedules, cash flow, and design cost exposure; identify cost and schedule impacts of design decisions and recommend mitigation.
Direct comprehensive design reviews, value engineering initiatives, peer reviews, and constructability assessments, balancing architectural integrity, technical performance, construction feasibility, cost, and schedule without compromising the intended design quality.
Oversee coordination of complex structural systems, building envelopes, waterproofing, MEP systems, highend architectural finishes, FF and E, IT/lowvoltage systems, and other ownerfurnished components, ensuring seamless integration across design, procurement, and construction disciplines.
Coordinate permitting and regulatory reviews with local authorities and technical consultants; proactively address schedule risks.
Lead procurement and contracting activities, including RFQ/RFP development, consultant and contractor prequalification, bid evaluation, negotiations, contract awards, and buyout. Develop procurement strategies addressing international sourcing, shipping logistics, limited local resources, and longlead materials and equipment.
Oversee consultant and contractor agreement administration, financial controls, invoice review, and tracking of budgeted, committed, actual, and projected costs. Evaluate commercial risks, proposed changes, and potential cost exposures to protect the client's financial interests.
Oversee project QA/QC procedures and risk and issue registers; proactively resolve technical, commercial, and logistical challenges.

Construction Management

Direct and oversee general contractors and multidisciplinary construction teams, lead OAC and project control group meetings, and assume primary responsibility for daytoday construction execution, including complex sequencing, site logistics, infrastructure coordination, and adherence to project quality, schedule, and budget objectives.
Provide seniorlevel technical oversight of construction activities, critically evaluating structural systems, building envelopes, waterproofing, MEP installations, construction methodologies, and highend architectural finishes. Proactively identify deficiencies, resolve complex field conditions, and direct consultants and contractors in implementing technically sound solutions.
Oversee the review and resolution of submittals, RFIs, shop drawings, substitution requests, change proposals, and change orders. Evaluate technical and commercial implications, challenge unnecessary costs or design complexities, and review and approve monthly payment requests in accordance with contractual requirements and delegated authority.
Direct construction quality assurance and quality control activities, oversee special inspections, site safety compliance, insurance requirements, construction schedules, and FF and E installation. Monitor contractor performance and enforce accountability for workmanship, coordination, and adherence to the project's luxury design and construction standards.
Oversee construction reporting and provide executive updates on milestones, financial performance, schedule risks, technical issues, and corrective actions.
Direct substantial completion and project closeout activities, including inspections, punch lists, occupancy approvals, commissioning, record drawings, warranties, contract closeouts, final payments, digital turnover, and coordination with hospitality operators and client representatives to ensure operational readiness and successful handover.
Other duties may be assigned.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

A minimum of a bachelor's degree in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, or a related technical field is required.
A minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible construction or project management experience.
Demonstrated experience managing complex, multidisciplinary design teams throughout the project life cycle.
Proven ability to independently lead major construction developments, manage sophisticated international project teams, exercise sound technical and commercial judgment, and effectively resolve complex design and construction challenges.

Must possess exceptional organizational, analytical, leadership, and problemsolving skills, with the ability to anticipate challenges, manage competing priorities, make independent decisions, and maintain accountability across multiple project disciplines.
Must have strong written communication skills and proficiency with project management, scheduling, document control, and construction management software.
Experience delivering complex projects in the Caribbean or comparable remote island environments is strongly preferred.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM
is seeking a Project Manager –Transmission & Distribution
with a passion for driving results to join our high-performing energy practice team.

In this role, the project manager will plan, direct, and execute moderate to large sized projects to support electric utilities. Our Project Managers are AECOM’s leaders readily managing, leading project teams, and delivering technical excellence, to provide client satisfaction through the use of structured processes and tools. This position will be on a REMOTE basis.

AECOM’s Energy practice provides a wide range of services from consulting and engineering design to energy engineering, energy procurement and construction (EPC) for power, energy efficiency, and renewable energy clients. Our understanding of the big picture – and the interconnection between generation, distribution, storage, and the demand side of the meter – allows us to deliver holistic strategies that improve and modernize next generation energy infrastructure. We connect knowledge and experience across our global framework to bring together a unique combination of engineers, planners, scientists, and project managers who advance cleaner, secure, and more sustainable energy solutions.

The job responsibilities of the position will include but are not limited to:
Use their strong working knowledge of transmission electric utilities to manage the full life cycle of substation or transmission projects.
Be responsible for design, permitting, construction, community engagement, and establishing/achieving critical project milestones.
Utilize your strong interpersonal, organizational, and creative problem-solving skills, to collaborate and lead project stake holders.
Work closely with the Project Team to confirm deliverables and services are being provided to exceed client’s satisfaction. This includes coordination with team members across the world.
Identify project opportunities early and facilitate go/no-go decisions, determine project fees, write proposals, prepare and lead client presentations, and negotiation of contracts.
Support development and maintenance of business plan; lead and support proposal efforts to support profitable growth.
Enjoy building teams, capturing new work, and growing Client relationships.
Take ownership of internal project financials, staffing, legal coordination, and risk management.
Be results-oriented with strong interpersonal, organizational, problem-solving, collaboration and leadership skills.
Enjoy managing projects that vary in size and complexity in multiple locations.

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements:

Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or related field and 4 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
Project Management experience directly related to transmission and substation engineering projects
Demonstrated experience delivering complex projects and/or programs with high quality on schedule and within scope and budget

Preferred Qualifications:

Masters Degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or related field
Project Management Professional (PMP)
5+ years of relevant experience, including project management program management engineering of transmission and substation work

Additional Information

Relocation assistance is not available for this role.
Sponsorship for US Employment Authorization is not available for this position.
THIS POSTING IS FOR A CURRENT VACANCY, AND AECOM INTENDS TO FILL THIS POSITION BY JANUARY 29, 2027.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $100000 to $140000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager II, Client Onboarding & Implementation
jobs.description:
Senior Project Manager II, Client Onboarding & Implementation-Full Time (Remote)

Our Organization

CDP, a Boston-based public benefit corporation, uses the collaborative fundraising model to improve the operational efficiency and revenue generation capacity of the public media system. CDP currently provides more than 230 NPR and PBS public media organizations (PMOs) with outsourced marketing, data analytics, fundraising, and technology services. These services help PMOs raise more net income, grow their donor files faster, lower their fundraising costs, and free up development talent allowing stations to better focus on local engagement. Since its inception, CDP has delivered more than $1 billion in membership revenue for local PMOs participating in its services and has become the most widely adopted Public Media service in the history of public broadcasting.

Just as CDP is committed to supporting public media organizations around the country, we are equally committed to supporting each of our team in their own professional development.

For more information, visit www.cdpcommunity.org.

Role Overview

The Enterprise Project Management Office is seeking a Sr. Project Manager to join our Client Onboarding Team. Onboarding plays a critical role in helping public media organizations achieve their mission. As the bridge between a station's decision to partner with CDP and their long-term success, the onboarding team helps clients adopt the tools, processes, and capabilities they need to strengthen fundraising, deepen audience engagement, and support the communities they serve. Every successful implementation enables our clients to focus more time and resources on delivering trusted journalism, educational content, and public service. In this role, you’ll guide client stations through one of the biggest organizational changes they’ll make: onboarding to CDP’s Member Services Bureau (MSB).

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys solving complex problems, building strong client partnerships, and navigating ambiguity. Every implementation is unique, requiring a balance of strategic thinking, adaptability, and hands-on execution. Beyond leading successful implementations, you’ll identify patterns across engagements, using those insights to help shape onboarding strategy, drive improvements, and translate lessons learned into better frameworks, decisions, and outcomes for every client that follows.

If you're energized by challenges, comfortable working through unknowns, passionate about continuous improvement, and motivated by helping clients achieve meaningful outcomes, you'll find this work deeply rewarding.

Key Responsibilities

Project Leadership

Lead end-to-end project management for multiple complex client implementations, from onboarding through go-live and post-launch support, serving as the primary point of contact throughout each engagement.

Coordinate work across internal teams and external partners to deliver a smooth transition for the station, driving delivery outcomes across scope, timeline, quality, and client experience.

Own the integrated project plan across all implementation workstreams (data conversion, marketing, operations, support, etc.), managing the critical path, handoffs, and interdependencies between workstreams, and adjusting the plan when changes in one area affect the rest.

Facilitate client-facing status meetings, internal check-ins, and milestone reviews to ensure alignment and progress.

Provide regular executive updates to keep leadership informed on progress, key milestones, blockers, and overall status.

Anticipate and resolve risks, issues, and cross-functional blockers before they impact project timelines.

Partner with subject-matter experts when technical, data, marketing, finance, or operational expertise is required, while retaining overall project ownership.

Stakeholder & Client Leadership

Build and maintain trusted relationships with client executives throughout the implementation lifecycle.

Lead complex client conversations and executive-level escalations, mitigating risks, and driving resolution while maintaining stakeholder confidence.

Guide clients through the adoption of new tools, platforms, workflows, and business processes by connecting implementation activities to operational outcomes and long-term business objectives.

Risk, Issue & Decision Leadership

Proactively identify red flags, assumptions, constraints, dependencies, and readiness gaps before they affect client outcomes.

Lead issue resolution across internal teams, station stakeholders, and external partners; remove blockers and drive decisions to closure.

Maintain current risk, issue, decision, and dependency records with clear impact, severity, ownership, mitigation, target dates, and escalation paths.

Escalate thoughtfully with a concise problem statement, business and client impact, actions already taken, viable options, and a recommendation.

Use trends and lessons learned across implementations to strengthen mitigation strategies and prevent repeat issues.

Provide proactive insights and recommendations that influence onboarding strategy and client outcomes.

Problem Discovery & Product-Oriented Thinking

Frame problems clearly, assess impact, engage the appropriate partners, and bring options and a recommended path forward.

Support journey mapping, current-state and future-state process mapping, and solution-shaping sessions when appropriate.

Distinguish project-specific issues from systemic patterns that may require broader product, operational, or organizational solutions.

Key Skills & Attributes

•10+ years of experience in Project Management, Client Onboarding, or SaaS/CRM implementations.

•Strong communication and relationship skills, including influencing and presenting to executive leadership.

•Exceptional problem-solving skills, intellectual curiosity, and a proven ability to quickly learn, adapt, and succeed in unfamiliar territory.

•Experience managing several concurrent projects and balancing priorities across a portfolio.

•A track record of leading complex, multi-workstream implementations and cross-functional strategic initiatives.

•Expertise with project management and collaboration tools (e.g., Smartsheet, Asana, Microsoft Teams).

•Committed to continuous improvement and operational excellence.

•Adept at navigating diverse project environments, dynamically applying Waterfall, Agile, or hybrid delivery models to optimize project outcomes.

•Familiarity with Lean and similar continuous improvement methodologies is a plus

Educational Requirements

•Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent work experience preferred.

Commitment to Inclusion

We strongly encourage individuals from historically marginalized and underrepresented groups to apply, even if you don’t meet every qualification. We value diverse perspectives, lived experiences, and commitment to public service. All CDP people have unique talents and experiences that create our company culture where we can all thrive and bring our whole selves to work each day.

Successful candidates will identify easily with a set of character attributes, as listed below:

• Inclusive mindset: You embrace and demonstrate an inclusion mindset and role model these behaviors for the organization.

• A Communicator: You possess strong communication skills and have great customer service skills; you like people and want to help.

• A Critical Thinker: You regularly look for ways to find efficiencies, innovate, and make improvements where you can.

• Process Oriented: You’re able to understand, work in, create, and improve processes.

• A Collaborator: You’re a team player willing to help where needed; a relationship builder whose can-do attitude inspires others; you actively share your job knowledge with team members.

• Someone Who Seeks to Learn: You are eager to listen, study, and learn new things quickly; you are resourceful and are open to regularly accepting and growing from feedback.

• Enterprising: You have proven success working in a fast-paced and changing environment; you have a strong work ethic and are excited to add value to the organization and its mission.

jobs.description:
Tetra Tech’s Water Team is seeking a municipal project manager/senior civil engineer to lead civil infrastructure projects while remaining closely engaged in technical design. This is a hybrid or remote opportunity in California. It is a client-facing position that supports a wide range of municipal work—including treatment facilities, storage, collection and conveyance systems, pump stations, drainage systems, and other water-related projects—helping strengthen a competitive municipal practice. This high-impact role is ideal for someone who excels at combining technical expertise, team leadership, and community-focused infrastructure solutions across California. This position augments a team that specializes in engineering public water systems to upgrade aging infrastructure, provide sustainable solutions, and develop innovative approaches to help preserve safe and reliable water delivery in California.

Your Impact

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to drive meaningful change worldwide. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

Serve as the primary client liaison for municipal clients, maintaining strong relationships and ensuring satisfaction.
Lead, perform, and manage projects that include water and wastewater treatment, distribution and transmission mains, wastewater collection, trunk and force main, pumping stations, wells, storage tanks, civil grading, drainage, as well as rehabilitation of existing infrastructure.
Guide teams on design and reporting to ensure high-quality, timely deliverables.
Ensure the team is aligned throughout the project delivery.
Apply technical expertise by performing design calculations and analysis, preparing detailed engineering reports, preparing construction documentation, and providing construction support services.
Scope projects, negotiate contracts, participate in business development activities, and represent Tetra Tech at industry events and oversee technical quality, budgets, and schedules.

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
Company Description

In September 2025, AUMOVIO emerged as a spin-off from Continental’s former Automotive group sector and has since established itself as an independent technology company. The company offers a broad portfolio for safe, exciting, connected and autonomous mobility, including sensor solutions, displays, brake and comfort systems as well as extensive expertise in software, architecture platforms and advanced driver assistance systems for software-defined vehicles. In fiscal year 2025, AUMOVIO generated sales of € 18.5 billion. Headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, AUMOVIO has around 82,000 employees at more than 80 locations worldwide.

Own What’s Next.

At AUMOVIO, we own what we do: Developing and producing hardware, software, and services that shape the future of mobility. But what truly sets us apart are our people. People who thrive in our winning culture, driven by bold ideas. People who take a leap and create meaningful differences together. Because we believe that the future belongs to those who own it. That’s why we foster a culture where you own every step of the way.

Own your career, your growth, your skills, and your impact. Join us and own what’s next.

Job Description

The Project Manager
owns engineering feasibility assessments, manufacturing/process design, validation plans, and integrated project plans for customer programs involving new automotive technologies, from project initiation through industrialization and successful launch. Working with engineering, manufacturing, and quality teams, this role applies engineering analysis to evaluate customer requirements, develop production-process solutions, assess product and process changes, and verify readiness against technical, quality, and manufacturing requirements. The Project Manager leads cross-functional project teams and remains accountable for program delivery, including timeline management, budget control, risk mitigation, resource coordination, and stakeholder communication. The role also supports business acquisition activities for assigned customers and serves as a key interface between customer organizations and internal functions.

This position is specifically allocated within our Business Growth Environment
, requiring a highly customer-focused professional. The successful candidate translates customer requirements, challenges, and strategic objectives into technically feasible product-development and industrialization plans, working with engineers to evaluate proposed solutions and change requests. By building strong customer partnerships, identifying growth potential, and aligning technical feasibility with manufacturing capability and commercial objectives, the Project Manager contributes to successful program execution and long-term business expansion.

Core Responsibilities

Serve as the primary customer contact across multiple products, communicating technical assessments and project status, coordinating cross-functional responses, managing expectations, and building strong relationships throughout the project lifecycle.
Act as the voice of the customer within the organization, translating customer needs into technical and operational requirements and aligning engineering, manufacturing, and project priorities.
Serve as the primary interface with the customer engineering team; own engineering feasibility assessments and work with engineers to evaluate technology-development requirements, technical alternatives, and proposed product or process changes.
Own manufacturing/process design and industrialization deliverables for assigned programs. Develop and evaluate process-design solutions with engineering and manufacturing teams, assessing how product requirements, production methods, resources, quality controls, and validation activities integrate to support reliable, efficient production. Coordinate application development, resource planning, schedules, risks and opportunities, budgets, and launch execution.
Analyze engineering specifications, technical and validation data, manufacturing capability, and commercial and project data to evaluate feasibility, identify product or process issues, and recommend engineering solutions. Assess the effects of proposed design and process changes on production cost, quality, reliability, resources, and launch readiness.
Ensure customer requirements are understood, documented, and evaluated against internal product, service, engineering, and manufacturing capabilities. Develop technically supported recommendations with engineers when customer requirements are immature or missing, and maintain alignment between requirements, process-design decisions, and validation criteria.
Lead a global cross-functional team of engineering, manufacturing, quality, sales, finance, and purchasing to develop and industrialize assigned technologies within defined scope, planned timing, and target budget. Own validation plans with engineering and quality teams, evaluate results against technical and quality requirements, and drive resolution of identified gaps while maintaining profitability and meeting customer milestones.
Establish project kickoff and integrated project baselines covering engineering feasibility, manufacturing/process design, validation deliverables, resources, timing, cost, and customer milestones. Maintain current technical decisions and project documentation throughout development and launch.
Establish monitoring mechanisms with the multidisciplinary project team to assess technical deliverables, validation progress, manufacturing readiness, and milestone performance. Develop corrective and recovery actions with engineering, manufacturing, and quality teams and escalate unresolved risks in time to avoid milestone delays.
Represent the project team to internal stakeholders, providing transparent reporting on engineering feasibility, technical decisions, validation results, industrialization readiness, project status, and unresolved risks.
Own project scope and engineering change-request assessments. Work with engineers to evaluate proposed product and process changes for technical feasibility and their effects on manufacturing methods, validation requirements, quality, reliability, production cost, resources, and timing. Develop documented technical recommendations, effort estimates, and execution plans, and ensure agreed customer changes are implemented and verified while meeting targeted margin objectives.
Manage project profitability and work with engineering and manufacturing teams to evaluate cost-effective product and process alternatives, reduce avoidable rework, and improve process efficiency while maintaining technical, quality, and customer requirements.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related field
Minimum 7 years of progressive experience in automotive development and project execution, including leading cross-functional delivery through industrialization and launch.
Within that experience, at least 5 years in customer-facing automotive project or engineering roles, communicating requirements, technical issues, changes, and program status.
Experience evaluating engineering feasibility, manufacturing/process readiness, validation results, and product/process change impacts.
Proficiency in project management tools (Microsoft Project or equivalent), MS PowerPoint, and MS Excel
Demonstrated ability to communicate technical and program information clearly to customers and internal stakeholders.
Ability to manage project plans, milestones, priorities, risks, documentation, and follow-up actions across multiple stakeholders.
Experience collaborating with global, cross-functional, or geographically distributed project teams.
Experience supporting automotive customers.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced automotive project development experience beyond the minimum qualifications.
Experience with complex electronic modules
Master’s degree in engineering, Business, or a related field.
Experience with traditional OEMs and New Mobility or similar OEM customer development, launch, or program management processes.
PMP certification.
Manufacturing interface experience / Build to Print experience
Efficiency improvement experience by process optimization, automation or AI

Additional Information

Legal authorization to work in the U.S. is required.
AUMOVIO may offer visa support for internal candidates who currently have a valid employment visa.
AUMOVIO does not offer relocation assistance for this opportunity.

What We Offer

Immediate Benefits
Robust Total Rewards Package
Paid Time Off
Volunteer Time Off
Employee Discounts
Competitive Bonus Programs
Employee 401k Match
Employee Assistance Program
Future Growth Opportunities, including personal and professional.
And many more benefits that come with working for a global industry leader!

EEO-Statement

EEO / AA / Disabled / Protected Veteran Employer. AUMOVIO offers equal employment opportunities to all qualified individuals, without regard to unlawful consideration to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, religion, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law. In addition, as a federal contractor, AUMOVIO complies with government regulations, where they apply, including affirmative action responsibilities for qualified individuals with a disability and protected veterans. To be considered, you must apply for a specific position for which AUMOVIO has a current posted job opening. Qualifying applications will be considered only for the specific opening(s) to which you apply. If you would like to be considered for additional or future job openings, we encourage you to reapply for other opportunities as they become available. Further, AUMOVIO provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with a disability.

Ready to take your career to the next level? The future of mobility isn’t just anyone’s job. Make it yours! Join AUMOVIO. Own What’s Next.
