Key Responsibilities

Project Leadership

Lead end-to-end project management for multiple complex client implementations, from onboarding through go-live and post-launch support, serving as the primary point of contact throughout each engagement.

Coordinate work across internal teams and external partners to deliver a smooth transition for the station, driving delivery outcomes across scope, timeline, quality, and client experience.

Own the integrated project plan across all implementation workstreams (data conversion, marketing, operations, support, etc.), managing the critical path, handoffs, and interdependencies between workstreams, and adjusting the plan when changes in one area affect the rest.

Facilitate client-facing status meetings, internal check-ins, and milestone reviews to ensure alignment and progress.

Provide regular executive updates to keep leadership informed on progress, key milestones, blockers, and overall status.

Anticipate and resolve risks, issues, and cross-functional blockers before they impact project timelines.

Partner with subject-matter experts when technical, data, marketing, finance, or operational expertise is required, while retaining overall project ownership.

Stakeholder & Client Leadership

Build and maintain trusted relationships with client executives throughout the implementation lifecycle.

Lead complex client conversations and executive-level escalations, mitigating risks, and driving resolution while maintaining stakeholder confidence.

Guide clients through the adoption of new tools, platforms, workflows, and business processes by connecting implementation activities to operational outcomes and long-term business objectives.

Risk, Issue & Decision Leadership

Proactively identify red flags, assumptions, constraints, dependencies, and readiness gaps before they affect client outcomes.

Lead issue resolution across internal teams, station stakeholders, and external partners; remove blockers and drive decisions to closure.

Maintain current risk, issue, decision, and dependency records with clear impact, severity, ownership, mitigation, target dates, and escalation paths.

Escalate thoughtfully with a concise problem statement, business and client impact, actions already taken, viable options, and a recommendation.

Use trends and lessons learned across implementations to strengthen mitigation strategies and prevent repeat issues.

Frame problems clearly, assess impact, engage the appropriate partners, and bring options and a recommended path forward.

Distinguish project-specific issues from systemic patterns that may require broader product, operational, or organizational solutions.

Key Skills & Attributes

•Exceptional problem-solving skills, intellectual curiosity, and a proven ability to quickly learn, adapt, and succeed in unfamiliar territory.

•Experience managing several concurrent projects and balancing priorities across a portfolio.

•A track record of leading complex, multi-workstream implementations and cross-functional strategic initiatives.

•Expertise with project management and collaboration tools (e.g., Smartsheet, Asana, Microsoft Teams).

•Committed to continuous improvement and operational excellence.

•Adept at navigating diverse project environments, dynamically applying Waterfall, Agile, or hybrid delivery models to optimize project outcomes.

•Familiarity with Lean and similar continuous improvement methodologies is a plus

Educational Requirements

At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future.

THE ROLE

We are seeking a Technical Program Manager to lead highly visible AI infrastructure programs focused on GPU platforms, rack-level solutions, and AI cluster validation. In this role, you will work across hardware, firmware, networking, systems, and validation teams to drive AI platforms from early system integration and bring-up through rack and cluster-scale readiness.

You will have the opportunity to work on complex AI infrastructure challenges spanning GPU and server integration, rack bring-up, scale testing, system debug, failure analysis, and deployment readiness. You will partner closely with engineering teams and senior leaders to turn complex technical dependencies into clear execution plans and help deliver reliable, scalable AI solutions for hyperscale and enterprise environments.

THE PERSON

You are a hands-on, technically curious program leader who thrives in complex, fast-moving engineering environments. You are comfortable diving into technical discussions while also maintaining a clear view of program priorities, risks, dependencies, and business outcomes.

You bring urgency, ownership, and structure to ambiguous problems and are skilled at bringing cross-functional teams together to drive decisions and execution. You can communicate effectively with engineers working through detailed system issues as well as senior leaders who need concise, data-driven program updates. You are also excited about finding new ways to improve engineering workflows through automation, Agentic AI, and AI-driven operational tools.

Lead coordination of platform and rack-level debug activities, helping teams rapidly triage issues, identify root causes, establish ownership, and drive issues to closure.
Track high-impact GPU, HSIO, firmware, rack, networking, and system failures through resolution.
Lead incident response for critical validation and deployment issues, including cross-functional debug efforts, escalation management, and executive communications.
Establish and track operational metrics such as Mean Time to Detect (MTTD), Mean Time to Mitigate (MTTM), Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR), incident recurrence, and fleet health.
Drive post-incident reviews, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and preventive measures to improve system reliability and deployment readiness.
Identify opportunities to apply Agentic AI and AIOps to engineering workflows, including automated triage, log analysis, root-cause identification, knowledge retrieval, test orchestration, and incident management.
Partner with data and engineering teams to integrate AI-powered operational tools and establish measurable success metrics for automation initiatives.
Provide clear, data-driven program updates to engineering teams and senior leadership while proactively escalating risks, dependencies, and critical tradeoffs.

Preferred Experience

Experience leading complex hardware, systems, AI infrastructure, or datacenter programs across bring-up, validation, and deployment.
Technical understanding of GPU-based AI systems, server platforms, rack architectures, and datacenter infrastructure.
Experience with GPU cluster scale testing, system stress testing, performance validation, or large-scale systems validation.

Experience working through hardware and firmware debug cycles in pre-production, validation, deployment, or customer-facing environments.
Experience coordinating cross-functional engineering teams and driving technical issues to closure without direct authority.
Experience with fleet-scale validation or deployment of AI, cloud, HPC, or hyperscale infrastructure.

Familiarity with Agentic AI, AIOps, or AI-enabled automation for engineering, validation, debug, or operational workflows.
Strong program management skills, including schedule management, dependency tracking, risk management, executive reporting, and cross-functional coordination.

new_jobs.title: Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

In September 2025, AUMOVIO emerged as a spin-off from Continental’s former Automotive group sector and has since established itself as an independent technology company. The company offers a broad portfolio for safe, exciting, connected and autonomous mobility, including sensor solutions, displays, brake and comfort systems as well as extensive expertise in software, architecture platforms and advanced driver assistance systems for software-defined vehicles. In fiscal year 2025, AUMOVIO generated sales of € 18.5 billion. Headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, AUMOVIO has around 82,000 employees at more than 80 locations worldwide.

Own What’s Next.

At AUMOVIO, we own what we do: Developing and producing hardware, software, and services that shape the future of mobility. But what truly sets us apart are our people. People who thrive in our winning culture, driven by bold ideas. People who take a leap and create meaningful differences together. Because we believe that the future belongs to those who own it. That’s why we foster a culture where you own every step of the way.

Own your career, your growth, your skills, and your impact. Join us and own what’s next.

Job Description

The Project Manager
owns engineering feasibility assessments, manufacturing/process design, validation plans, and integrated project plans for customer programs involving new automotive technologies, from project initiation through industrialization and successful launch. Working with engineering, manufacturing, and quality teams, this role applies engineering analysis to evaluate customer requirements, develop production-process solutions, assess product and process changes, and verify readiness against technical, quality, and manufacturing requirements. The Project Manager leads cross-functional project teams and remains accountable for program delivery, including timeline management, budget control, risk mitigation, resource coordination, and stakeholder communication. The role also supports business acquisition activities for assigned customers and serves as a key interface between customer organizations and internal functions.

This position is specifically allocated within our Business Growth Environment
, requiring a highly customer-focused professional. The successful candidate translates customer requirements, challenges, and strategic objectives into technically feasible product-development and industrialization plans, working with engineers to evaluate proposed solutions and change requests. By building strong customer partnerships, identifying growth potential, and aligning technical feasibility with manufacturing capability and commercial objectives, the Project Manager contributes to successful program execution and long-term business expansion.

Core Responsibilities

Serve as the primary customer contact across multiple products, communicating technical assessments and project status, coordinating cross-functional responses, managing expectations, and building strong relationships throughout the project lifecycle.
Act as the voice of the customer within the organization, translating customer needs into technical and operational requirements and aligning engineering, manufacturing, and project priorities.
Serve as the primary interface with the customer engineering team; own engineering feasibility assessments and work with engineers to evaluate technology-development requirements, technical alternatives, and proposed product or process changes.
Own manufacturing/process design and industrialization deliverables for assigned programs. Develop and evaluate process-design solutions with engineering and manufacturing teams, assessing how product requirements, production methods, resources, quality controls, and validation activities integrate to support reliable, efficient production. Coordinate application development, resource planning, schedules, risks and opportunities, budgets, and launch execution.
Analyze engineering specifications, technical and validation data, manufacturing capability, and commercial and project data to evaluate feasibility, identify product or process issues, and recommend engineering solutions. Assess the effects of proposed design and process changes on production cost, quality, reliability, resources, and launch readiness.
Ensure customer requirements are understood, documented, and evaluated against internal product, service, engineering, and manufacturing capabilities. Develop technically supported recommendations with engineers when customer requirements are immature or missing, and maintain alignment between requirements, process-design decisions, and validation criteria.
Lead a global cross-functional team of engineering, manufacturing, quality, sales, finance, and purchasing to develop and industrialize assigned technologies within defined scope, planned timing, and target budget. Own validation plans with engineering and quality teams, evaluate results against technical and quality requirements, and drive resolution of identified gaps while maintaining profitability and meeting customer milestones.
Establish project kickoff and integrated project baselines covering engineering feasibility, manufacturing/process design, validation deliverables, resources, timing, cost, and customer milestones. Maintain current technical decisions and project documentation throughout development and launch.
Establish monitoring mechanisms with the multidisciplinary project team to assess technical deliverables, validation progress, manufacturing readiness, and milestone performance. Develop corrective and recovery actions with engineering, manufacturing, and quality teams and escalate unresolved risks in time to avoid milestone delays.
Represent the project team to internal stakeholders, providing transparent reporting on engineering feasibility, technical decisions, validation results, industrialization readiness, project status, and unresolved risks.
Own project scope and engineering change-request assessments. Work with engineers to evaluate proposed product and process changes for technical feasibility and their effects on manufacturing methods, validation requirements, quality, reliability, production cost, resources, and timing. Develop documented technical recommendations, effort estimates, and execution plans, and ensure agreed customer changes are implemented and verified while meeting targeted margin objectives.
Manage project profitability and work with engineering and manufacturing teams to evaluate cost-effective product and process alternatives, reduce avoidable rework, and improve process efficiency while maintaining technical, quality, and customer requirements.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related field
Minimum 7 years of progressive experience in automotive development and project execution, including leading cross-functional delivery through industrialization and launch.
Within that experience, at least 5 years in customer-facing automotive project or engineering roles, communicating requirements, technical issues, changes, and program status.
Experience evaluating engineering feasibility, manufacturing/process readiness, validation results, and product/process change impacts.
Proficiency in project management tools (Microsoft Project or equivalent), MS PowerPoint, and MS Excel
Demonstrated ability to communicate technical and program information clearly to customers and internal stakeholders.
Ability to manage project plans, milestones, priorities, risks, documentation, and follow-up actions across multiple stakeholders.
Experience collaborating with global, cross-functional, or geographically distributed project teams.
Experience supporting automotive customers.

Preferred Qualifications

Advanced automotive project development experience beyond the minimum qualifications.
Experience with complex electronic modules
Master’s degree in engineering, Business, or a related field.
Experience with traditional OEMs and New Mobility or similar OEM customer development, launch, or program management processes.
PMP certification.
Manufacturing interface experience / Build to Print experience
Efficiency improvement experience by process optimization, automation or AI

Additional Information

Legal authorization to work in the U.S. is required.
AUMOVIO may offer visa support for internal candidates who currently have a valid employment visa.
AUMOVIO does not offer relocation assistance for this opportunity.

What We Offer

Immediate Benefits
Robust Total Rewards Package
Paid Time Off
Volunteer Time Off
Employee Discounts
Competitive Bonus Programs
Employee 401k Match
Employee Assistance Program
Future Growth Opportunities, including personal and professional.
And many more benefits that come with working for a global industry leader!

EEO-Statement

EEO / AA / Disabled / Protected Veteran Employer. AUMOVIO offers equal employment opportunities to all qualified individuals, without regard to unlawful consideration to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, religion, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law. In addition, as a federal contractor, AUMOVIO complies with government regulations, where they apply, including affirmative action responsibilities for qualified individuals with a disability and protected veterans. To be considered, you must apply for a specific position for which AUMOVIO has a current posted job opening. Qualifying applications will be considered only for the specific opening(s) to which you apply. If you would like to be considered for additional or future job openings, we encourage you to reapply for other opportunities as they become available. Further, AUMOVIO provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with a disability.

Ready to take your career to the next level? The future of mobility isn’t just anyone’s job. Make it yours! Join AUMOVIO. Own What’s Next.

to lead complex digital programs and strategic client engagements. This role is ideal for an experienced delivery leader who thrives in fast-paced environments, excels at stakeholder management, and brings a strong balance of operational rigor, client partnership, and business acumen.

Brief Description

Job Title:
Program Manager

Clearance Required:
US Citizen, Active Secret

Work Location:
Hybrid; Washington, DC (3 days onsite required)

Alpha Omega is looking for a focused, driven Program Manager (PM) that will have overall delivery responsibility for the tasks and activities to include Contractor team performance and issue resolution. The PM will factor in all inputs to derive a recommended approach based on factors including prioritization and subject matter expertise, technical and business information, risk management, and industry best practices.

Key Responsibilities

Demonstrated Program/Project Management experience in an Agile environment
Experience with software and cybersecurity requirements tools and tracking
Experience working and leading an Agile Program with multiple work streams /components.
Experience defining solutions that cross business and technical boundaries.
Experience monitoring program execution to identify obstacles and deviations from plan and takes corrective action as needed
Experience conducting continuous risk assessment and management including developing measures to reduce risk in program execution
Experience with contract management, budgeting, and resource allocation, including management of subcontractor personnel
Experience with all aspects of configuration management planning including configuration identification, change control, configuration status accounting, configuration audits, configuration documentation
Manage a team of resources across the various projects on the program.
Communicate with stakeholders and customers who are involved with projects on the program
Demonstrate an understanding of IT infrastructure, including physical and virtual servers, operating systems, networks, storage, databases, backups, and the dependencies between infrastructure and applications.
Demonstrate an understanding of cloud technologies and experience managing or supporting teams operating in cloud, on-premises, and hybrid environments, including coordination of cloud operations, system availability, security, and modernization activities.
Lead integrated teams responsible for application development and maintenance, infrastructure operations, database administration, cybersecurity, service desk support, and other technical services across multiple work streams.
Oversee operations and maintenance activities, including system monitoring, incident and problem resolution, patching, performance management, change coordination, and service restoration to support the availability and reliability of mission-critical systems.
Coordinate cybersecurity and compliance activities, including continuous monitoring, vulnerability remediation, Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) compliance, Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), and activities supporting system Assessments and Authorizations and Authorities to Operate (ATOs).
Partner with government system owners, Information System Security Officers (ISSOs), technical teams, and other stakeholders to identify dependencies, prioritize risks, and coordinate remediation and authorization activities.
Establish and maintain a strong working relationship with the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR), government leadership, and other stakeholders through proactive communication, transparency, and timely resolution of issues.
Translate customer priorities into actionable work plans, clearly defined responsibilities, measurable milestones, and prioritized backlogs; regularly communicate progress, risks, decisions, and resource needs.
Oversee contract deliverables, reporting, and performance against the Performance Work Statement or Statement of Work, Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP), and applicable service-level and performance requirements.
Lead change and release management activities, coordinating with government stakeholders and technical teams to assess impacts, obtain required approvals, and minimize disruption to production systems and users.
Manage staffing, onboarding, access, and succession planning to maintain qualified personnel, continuity of operations, and appropriate coverage across program functions.
Use performance metrics, customer feedback, and operational trends to identify improvement opportunities, strengthen service delivery, and demonstrate measurable program outcomes.
Provide clear direction and accountability across the team, facilitate collaboration, coach personnel, and address performance or customer concerns promptly and constructively.

Required Experience/Skills
:

Minimum Years of Overall Experience: Twelve (12) or more years of relevant experience in an Enterprise IT environment leading major systems support and integration efforts across a mixed platform
Minimum Years of Specific Experience in Field: 5 or more years of relevant experience working in Federal Government
Strong and effective verbal and communications skills
Exceptional leadership and organizational skills

Shall have, at a minimum, a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology Management or Engineering, or other comparable degree or experience

An active PMI Project Management Professional (PMP®) or PMI Program Management Professional (PgMP®) Certification
ITIL v3 or higher

The likely salary range for this position is $145,000 - $175,000. This is not, however, a guarantee of compensation or salary. January 28, 2027

Joining the Alpha Omega team entitles you to participate in all retirement benefits, plans of deferred compensation, health and insurance benefits, and other such benefits as set forth in the company’s policy and benefits manuals. See below, to name a few:

15 days PTO including paid parental, military, and bereavement leave
Eleven (11) paid Federal holidays, five of which are floating holidays (as designated by the company’s holiday schedule each year)
Health and Dental Insurance (including 100% employer paid premiums for employee coverage under the HDHP health plan)
Life Insurance, STD/LTD term disability coverage, with employer paid premiums
401 (k) plan with a match that is 100% vested after you complete two years of service

Alpha Omega is an award-winning solutions provider dedicated to delivering mission-enabling technology and strategic solutions for our customers. Since our founding in 2016, we have grown to over 700 employees nationwide consisting of former operators, technologists, and strategists who bring decades of government and industry experience. They are united by one purpose: ensuring our nation’s continued global leadership.

We have a unified operating model providing technical capabilities and solutions for customers across two main business units:

National Security – supporting agencies such as the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Navy, Air Force, Army, and the Department of State (DOS).

Through strategic partnerships, intellectual property, and relentless drive for innovation, Alpha Omega is shaping the future of government technology. We are proud to be a Virginia Best Places to Work 8 times, an Inc. 5000 honoree 7 times, and a Washington Post Top Workplaces 4 times. Join us in driving transformation that secures the nation's future.

Culture And Values

Guided by our core values—Harmony, Engagement, Accountability, Resourcefulness, and Tenacity (HEART)— we foster a culture of innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning and are committed to delivering high-impact solutions. We recognize and reward hard work.

Alpha Omega's culture is driven by our values and mission. We invest in top talent through mentorship, growth, and meaningful work. We value individuality, reward integrity, and foster a diverse, high-performing team united by purpose-at work, in service, and in the community.

Securitas Security Services USA, Inc. is the global leader in protective services, delivering specialized guarding, advanced technology solutions, and comprehensive risk management to clients across a wide range of industries. As a Health & Safety Program Manager, you will be responsible for supporting and driving Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) performance in a fast-paced, dynamic environment where your decisions directly influence outcomes. With modern technology and a strong local team, you’ll design and manage safety programs tailored to unique client needs while owning both operational performance and risk management results.

The ideal candidate is a proactive safety leader who builds strong relationships with stakeholders, communicates clearly under pressure, and uses data to drive continuous improvement.

Strategic Leadership & Program Management

Ensure governing directives such as OSHA and other applicable regulations are followed.

Identify opportunities for process improvement and recommend changes to workflow and operating practices to improve efficiency.
Perform other duties as assigned to ensure the overall success of the Datacenter Physical Security & Safety program.

Incident & Risk Management

Remotely provide expert incident management for injuries, from intake through root cause analysis and presentation of corrective action items.
Take escalations for EHS at any time, including weekends and holidays.
Provide timely, accurate communications to stakeholders when escalations are required.
Conduct annual review of safety-related documents in partnership with stakeholders.

Maintain a customer service approach to problem solving and work with the client to find solutions to questions or concerns.
Schedule and facilitate client and internal meetings using client meeting technology.

Ensure proper EHS document retention in line with client and company requirements.
Perform additional duties as assigned.

An ideal candidate brings:

A service-first mindset, clear communication skills, strong attention to detail, and sound judgment when approaching challenges.
A solutions-focused approach and the ability to thrive in both independent and team settings.
Comfort working in a fast-paced environment with frequent stakeholder interaction and occasional off-hours escalations.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Environmental Science, or a related field; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Certifications

Professional safety certifications (such as CSP, ASP, CHST) are preferred.

Skills And Experience

Experience with Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) programs and OSHA or similar regulatory frameworks.
Strong skills in Power BI and Excel for data analysis, reporting, and dashboard creation.
Ability to develop and deliver professional presentations to senior stakeholders.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including incident reporting and escalation communication.
Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities in a dynamic environment.
Strong relationship-building skills with clients, field operations, and cross-functional teams.
Experience in EHS program management within datacenter, technology, or critical infrastructure environments is preferred.
Knowledge of datacenter operations, physical security, or related industries is a plus.
Experience with remote incident management and multi-site EHS support is beneficial.

Why you would want to join the team

Direct impact on the safety and well-being of employees and contractors in a critical datacenter environment.
Regular interaction with high-level client stakeholders and Securitas leadership.
Opportunities to grow within Securitas’ broader Health & Safety and operational leadership structure.
Supportive leadership and a collaborative team focused on continuous improvement and learning.
Exposure to advanced technology environments and complex EHS challenges.
A strong partnership with the client and a culture that values proactive safety and clear communication.

Health & Safety Program Manager / Securitas Security / Dallas, TX / TXDPS #B03946

Securitas USA employees come from all walks of life, bringing a variety of skills, experiences, and perspectives. United by a shared purpose, we help make the world a safer place. We provide security services to meet the unique needs of our clients to help safeguard their people and assets.

Target salary range: $150k - $170k
. The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position based on experience and other factors.

Information Systems Security Manager

Department: Information Management

Clearance Requirement: Secret

Reports To: Chief Information Officer

Position Summary

The ISSM owns the security posture of JANUS corporate and CUI systems. You keep us compliant with RMF, NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-171, and CMMC Level 2. You also bring hands-on technical depth across Microsoft 365, AWS, Windows, Linux, and Active Directory.

This is a hybrid role that combines cybersecurity compliance oversight with system security and user training coordination.

The Cybersecurity Compliance Administrator will work closely with DCSA, the Facility Security Officer (FSO), external MSP, MSSP, service providers, and organizational leadership to ensure corporate systems remain secure and compliant.

Key Responsibilities

Maintain and update cybersecurity documentation, including SSPs, POA&Ms, policies, procedures, and user access records.
Implement and monitor security controls for NIST SP 800-171, NIST SP 800-53, and CMMC Level 2. Run continuous monitoring, collect evidence, and report risk to leadership.
Monitor and analyze Microsoft 365, including GCC High: Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, and Entra ID. Review Conditional Access, MFA, privileged roles, and Defender, Purview, and Intune findings.
Lead preparation for CMMC assessments, DCSA reviews, and audits. Work with DCSA, the FSO, service providers, and leadership.
Contribute to security audits, assessments, and continuous monitoring processes.
Coordinate and deliver end-user cybersecurity and IT training (e.g., phishing awareness, acceptable use).
Support onboarding/offboarding and system access management.
Assist with patch management, system hardening, and endpoint configurations.
Own the secure development program. Run SAST, DAST, and dependency scanning tools (such as Snyk, SonarQube, OWASP ZAP, or Burp Suite) in CI/CD pipelines, and triage findings with developers.
Assess AWS security (commercial and GovCloud): IAM, Security Hub, GuardDuty, CloudTrail, and AWS Config. Confirm that cloud services meet FedRAMP Moderate (or equivalent) before they hold CUI.
Assess Windows and Active Directory security: STIG and CIS baselines, Group Policy, privileged groups, tiered administration, service accounts, LAPS, BitLocker, and application control. Monitor for identity attacks.
Assess Linux security (RHEL and similar): STIG and CIS hardening, such as FIPS, LUKS, application and privilege access control, and logging (auditd). Run and review SCAP scans and remediating when necessary.

Required Qualifications

U.S. Citizenship and ability to obtain or maintain a DoD Security Clearance
3+ years of experience in IT systems, cybersecurity, or compliance support
Knowledge of NIST SP 800-171, CMMC Level 2, and RMF standards
Prior interaction with DCSA and knowledge of FSO/ISSM support requirements
Microsoft 365 administration experience (Entra ID, Teams, SharePoint, Exchange)
Security+ or equivalent IAM Level I certification (per DoD 8570)
Excellent communication, documentation, and organizational skills

Preferred Qualifications

IAM Level II Certification (CISSP, CISM, CCNA Sec, etc.)
Experience supporting DoD contractors or working in a cleared facility environment
Experience with virtualization technologies like VMWare vSphere, Hyper-V, and KVM/QEMU
Experience with containerized compute solutions like Docker, Podman, and Kubernetes
Familiarity with Microsoft Intune, Defender, and compliance features
Experience developing or managing cybersecurity training programs
Experience supporting developers using Python and C for development, and Terraform and Ansible for deployment

new_jobs.title: Program Manager, Enterprise Risk Management
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The Program Manager, Enterprise Risk Management, reports directly to the Director, Enterprise Risk Management. This role supports and advances CapMetro's Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) program through the execution of enterprise-wide risk identification, assessment, monitoring, reporting, and continuous improvement activities. This position works collaboratively with executives, department leaders, project teams, and other stakeholders to facilitate risk assessments, maintain the enterprise risk inventory, monitor risks and opportunities, develop reports, dashboards, and presentations, and coordinate ERM activities. The Operational Lead provides consultative guidance, tools, and expertise to business units while serving in a facilitative and advisory capacity to support effective risk management. The position supports the Organizational Strategy & Projects leadership team in embedding risk-informed decision-making and fostering a risk-aware culture through sound risk management practices and program enhancement.

Responsibilities

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

Note: The duties and primary responsibilities below are intended to describe the general content of and requirements of this job and are not intended to be an exhaustive statement of duties. 

Enterprise Risk Management Program Administration

Support the implementation, governance, and continuous improvement of CapMetro’s Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) program, including risk appetite, risk tolerance, policies, procedures, tools, metrics, and templates.
Drive the integration of risk analysis, management, and recommendations into strategic planning, organizational objectives, and business decision-making.
Develop and deliver enterprise risk reporting, dashboards, risk maps, trend analyses, and executive, Board, and governance communications.
Maintain ERM program documentation, risk records, templates, reporting artifacts, and document repositories, ensuring accuracy, completeness, version control, and retention of program information.

Risk Identification, Assessment, Prioritization, and Monitoring

Maintain the enterprise risk register, facilitate enterprise and departmental risk assessments, and identify, assess, prioritize, and communicate risks and opportunities affecting strategic and operational objectives.
Monitor risk trends, emerging risks, key risk indicators (KRIs), and enterprise exposures against established risk appetite and tolerance thresholds, escalating material deviations as appropriate.
Develop and enhance risk monitoring and mitigation practices, including early warning systems, preventive controls, mitigation tracking, post-event reviews, lessons learned, and continuous improvement of risk management processes.

Business Partnership, Culture, and Influence

Foster a culture of risk awareness, collaboration, and transparency through stakeholder engagement, education, coaching, and constructive communication.
Partner with business leaders and serve as a trusted advisor to facilitate informed risk-based decision-making while reinforcing business ownership and accountability for risk.
Support change management and organizational transition initiatives by guiding cross-functional teams through the adoption of new processes, tools, and analytical practices, helping facilitate workforce readiness, user adoption, and successful integration of risk management into organizational decision-making and ERM objectives.
Promote analytical rigor and risk-informed thinking by developing organizational capabilities, methodologies, and practices that strengthen risk analysis, support data-driven decision-making, and embed risk discipline across the organization.

Strategic Project & Capital Program Risk Support

Partner with strategic initiative, capital project, program, and portfolio teams to assess, review, and manage risks associated with major capital investments and strategic initiatives, promoting cross-functional integrated risk management and informed decision-making.
Facilitate project risk workshops and monitor risk mitigation activities to support effective project risk management and decision-making.

Organizational Stewardship

Perform responsibilities in a manner that supports CapMetro's mission, values, strategic goals, and commitment to organizational excellence.
Support Capital Metropolitan Transportation Authority’s Safety Management Systems (SMS) process by following safety and security policies, considering safety in every action and reporting safety and security concerns.
Perform other duties as required and/or assigned in support of the CapMetro Strategic Plan.

Qualifications

WHAT YOU BRING

Bachelor’s degree in risk management, business, economics, finance, public administration, management, or related field.
Eight (8) years of relevant experience in risk management, audit, compliance, governance, strategic planning, public administration, or related disciplines, including three (3) years of experience leading enterprise assessments, governance initiatives, and cross-functional business programs, with two (2) years of management experience managing employees or projects.
Preferred - Professional risk management qualification such as Certified Risk Management Professional (CRMP), Certification in Risk Management Assurance (CRMA), Enterprise Risk Manager (ERM), International Certificate in Enterprise Risk Management (IRM), Financial Risk Manager (FRM).
Preferred - Experience in public transportation, infrastructure, utilities, government, aviation, or large capital project environments.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Comprehensive knowledge of Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) principles, frameworks, and practices, including risk appetite, risk tolerance, and industry standards such as COSO ERM and ISO 31000.
Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to perform qualitative and quantitative risk analysis, identify trends, evaluate impacts, and synthesize data from multiple sources to support decision-making.
Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, deliverables, and program documentation in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to develop, maintain, and continuously improve systems, processes, documentation, and records that support effective risk management and program operations.
Proficiency in developing reports, dashboards, presentations, and other communication materials that effectively convey risk information and recommendations.
Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, and SharePoint, with experience developing reporting tools, dashboards, document repositories, and executive-level presentations.
Excellent verbal, written, presentation, and facilitation skills, including the ability to communicate complex concepts to diverse technical and non-technical audiences and adapt messaging to stakeholder needs.
Ability to influence, collaborate, build consensus, and maintain productive working relationships across all levels of the organization, while exercising sound judgment, professionalism, initiative, and a commitment to continuous learning and improvement.

WORK ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL DEMANDS

Work is generally performed in an office environment in which there is only minimal exposure to unpleasant and/or hazardous working conditions. This position works with multiple project timelines and performs work of a complex nature.

Incumbent must have the ability to stand and sit frequently throughout an eight-hour period, reach vertically for overhead use as well as horizontally. Must be able to use a telephone or headset equipment. Incumbents must be able to lift and move material weighing up to 20 lbs., perform work at a computer terminal for 6-8 hours a day, and function in an environment with constant interruptions. Regular and predictable attendance at assigned work location is an essential function.

Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disability to perform the essential functions as previously described.

WORK AUTHORIZATION

Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. All applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States.

Mobility Status

As a Hybrid position, onsite presence is guided by team collaboration needs, customer and front-line team member interactions, and role responsibilities. People leaders will set expectations for onsite presence; however, incumbents are generally encouraged to work 8 to 12 days in office per month. Mobility status is subject to change at any time based on business needs or organizational decisions.

COMMITMENT TO EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

CapMetro is an equal employment opportunity employer and committed to creating a welcoming environment for all employees. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, pregnancy, age, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. CapMetro makes hiring decisions based solely on qualifications, merit, and organization needs at the time.

new_jobs.title: Lead Program Manager Facilities Safety
new_jobs.description:
About Us

Every day we deliver safe and secure energy to homes, communities, and businesses. We are there when people need us the most. We connect people to the energy they need for the lives they live. The pace of change in society and our industry is accelerating and our expertise and track record puts us in an unparalleled position to shape the sustainable future of our industry. To be successful we must anticipate the needs of our customers, reducing the cost of energy delivery today and pioneering the flexible energy systems of tomorrow. This requires us to deliver on our promises and always look for new opportunities to grow, both ourselves and our business.

At National Grid, we aim to create an environment where everyone is welcomed for who they are and where our differences are celebrated. We utilize the insights of our employees that come from all different cultures, backgrounds, and beliefs to better serve our customers and communities.

National Grid is hiring a Lead Program Manager Facilities Safety. This role can sit in either our Northboro MA or Waltham MA location, but will require travel throughout the MA region.

Job Purpose

Lead the Property Services organization Safety Programs that include Emergency Action Planning (EAP), Shelter-In-Place (SIP), Business Continuity, Fire Life Safety, emergency preparedness, regulatory compliance, contractor safety oversight, and related facilities safety initiatives. Develop, maintain, implement, and continuously improve safety and emergency management programs to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, corporate standards, and industry best practices. Act as the single point of contact for emergency preparedness, life safety compliance, business continuity planning, and corporate safety audits across the Property Services business territory in a consistent manner. Serve as key member of Facilities team, partnering across the organization to drive progress against strategic initiatives and emerging needs.

Key Accountabilities

Translate NG US Emergency Planning policies and create Emergency Action Plan (EAP) standard operating processes and procedures for all Property Services locations, driving quality and awareness for NG stakeholders. Ensure compliance with regulations and internal standards while developing a culture of emergency preparedness. Conduct annual reviews of all EAPs and create tracking and reporting dashboards to validate compliance.
Emergency Action Planning (EAP) will include overall program development, participant assignment, training, compliance monitoring, annual reviews, reporting, tabletop exercises, evacuation drills, stakeholder engagement, and continuous improvement activities. Ensure stakeholders are trained and have conducted exercises in preparation of emergencies.
Create/conduct annual reviews of the Shelter-In-Place (SIP) program, including development of standard processes and procedures, identification of designated shelter locations, training and awareness activities, coordination with emergency responders, compliance monitoring, and reporting.
Work with Fire Wardens, Facilities Management, Communications teams, and site leadership to coordinate, manage, and execute fire drills and emergency exercises. Monitor drill performance, document corrective actions, and communicate lessons learned to improve emergency preparedness.
Work with the US Property Services teams to translate National Grid Business Continuity objectives into operating processes and procedures. Ensure compliance with regulations and internal standards and create a tracking and reporting dashboard to validate compliance.
Review/audit existing Business Continuity Plans (BCPs) for significant organizational, operational, facility, or personnel changes. Ensure appropriate business contacts, recovery strategies, and critical business information remain current. Coordinate review and approval with Management prior to final plan completion.
Audit and review existing Emergency Plans, Shelter-In-Place Plans, Business Continuity Plans, processes, and procedures and seek ways to improve effectiveness, efficiencies, strengthen compliance, and enhance emergency response capabilities.
Review all Health and Safety Plans (HASPs) as part of the approval workflow to ensure required safety accommodations, emergency response provisions, and regulatory requirements have been incorporated prior to submission to the Field Safety team for final review and approval.
Monitor activities such as maintenance of databases, delivery of training, emergency exercises, fire drills, compliance documentation, corrective actions, program progress, and emergency planning event schedules to ensure improvements are implemented and sustained.
Routinely review Fire Life Safety Policy to ensure alignment with government requirements and NG standards and communicate and operationalize changes as needed.

Cont'd Key Accountabilities

Conduct periodic audits to verify facilities maintain required fire code credentials, permits, certifications, and documentation. Develop and maintain inventories of fire department lock boxes, emergency equipment, and associated building locations to support compliance and emergency response readiness.
Conduct audits and maintain inventories of Emergency Evacuation Maps located throughout facilities to ensure maps accurately depict Emergency Action Plans (EAPs), evacuation routes, exits, Shelter-In-Place areas, and other life safety features. Establish ongoing review processes to maintain accuracy and compliance.
Coordinate with Facilities Management and Integrated Property Services (IPS) Partner to identify, document, and maintain inventories of all confined spaces within NG facilities. Ensure compliance with OSHA regulations, permit requirements, signage standards, and inspection protocols. Conduct reviews to verify signage continues to meet regulatory obligations.
Audit IPS Partner compliance programs and the preventative maintenance platform to verify adherence to NG policies, inspection schedules, corrective action requirements, and safety procedures. Ensure contractor-reported activities are being completed as documented and proactively address findings before they are identified by National Grid Safety teams.
Provide business continuity management training and advice to US Property Services management in the preparation of emergency and continuity plans to ensure improvements are implemented.
Create and implement the Shelter-In-Place program which includes but is not limited to identifying spaces within facilities, training local employees, and working with local emergency first responders to ensure program effectiveness and readiness.
Assist with the development of the Site Staging Program and support emergency response and operational continuity objectives.
Conduct facility safety audits to verify required building identification labels, emergency signage, life safety markings, and Automated External Defibrillator (AED) location signage are properly installed, maintained, visible, and compliant.
Develop and maintain program dashboards, tracking tools, and compliance reports to provide visibility into program effectiveness, audit performance, corrective actions, and overall safety readiness.

Qualifications

Degree qualified with knowledge and up to 5 years’ experience with fields relating to Business Continuity, Corporate Safety, Facilities and Emergency Planning. Demonstrates the ability to apply and modify theories and learned concepts appropriately. Demonstrates knowledge of the US utility business is a plus.
Experience of managing the work of a project with a similar size impact and preferably a project team. Demonstrates taking specific actions to enable stakeholders in a matrix environment to effectively and efficiently to achieve goals.
Understands theory behind policies and processes and demonstrates the ability to challenge existing processes and ways of working i.e., taking action to avoid future crisis or create opportunities to improve existing practices.
Detailed knowledge and understanding of the regulatory issues affecting the industry. Demonstrates the ability to anticipate obstacles and think ahead about next steps.
Demonstrates the ability network internally and externally and to develop successful, long-lasting business relationships / partnerships with others and seeks to understand and challenge business scenarios to the benefit of all parties.
Has proven program management ability to create, train and maintain similar programs across a large organization.
Education: Degree preferred in Emergency Management
A valid driver’s license is required
Travel throughout region required.

Salary

$130,000 - $152,000 a year

National Grid will not be providing visa sponsorship for this position now or in the future. You must have the ability to work without a need for current or future visa sponsorship.

National Grid utilizes an assessment that evaluates the job qualifications/characteristics using AI or statistically based scoring. For more information, please view NYC Local Law 144.

This position has a career path which provides for advancement opportunities within and across bands as you develop and evolve in the position; gaining experience, expertise and acquiring and applying technical skills. Candidates will be assessed and provided offers against the minimum qualifications of this role and their individual experience.

À la tête des entreprises qui s’engagent vers un avenir plus vert, Alstom développe et commercialise des solutions de mobilité qui apportent les fondements durables pour l'avenir des transports. Notre portefeuille de produits s'étend des trains à grande vitesse, métros, monorails et tramways jusqu’aux systèmes intégrés, services sur mesure, infrastructures, signalisation et solutions de mobilité numérique. Nous rejoindre, c'est rejoindre une entreprise bienveillante, responsable et innovante où plus de 70 000 personnes ouvrent la voie à une mobilité plus verte et plus intelligente, dans le monde entier.

TITRE DE POSTE : CRA Transformation Deputy Project Manager (F/M/X)

Localisation : Villeurbanne (69)

Votre futur role

Relevez un nouveau défi et mettez à profit votre expertise dans les domaines de la cybersécurité et du juridique dans un nouveau domaine de pointe. Vous travaillerez avec une équipe dynamique et innovante et vous jouerez un rôle clé dans la transformation de l’entreprise et la protection de nos produits électroniques contre les menaces numériques.

Au sein de l’équipe de transformation, vous travaillerez au quotidien en étroite collaboration avec l’ensemble des équipes œuvrant à la mise en conformité de l’entreprise au Cybersecurity Resilience Act (CRA), soit les équipes de cybersécurité et de développement de produits, des projets ainsi que les équipes transverses (juridique, achats, supply chain, certification et autorisation, etc.).

Vous vous occuperez plus particulièrement du suivi de la mise en conformité des Produits comportant des éléments numériques (PDE en anglais), de l’accompagnement de la transformation des différents services de l’entreprise, de la gestion des risques, et du reporting vers la gouvernance du projet.

Nous ferons appel à vous pour :

Aider à l’interprétation de la loi
Coordonner la centralisation des données de conformité dans un outil dédié
Gérer les registres des actions et de des risques
Définir et construire les différents indicateurs de conformité
Définir les modèles de reporting
Contribuer à la préparation des comités de pilotage

Votre profil

Nous accordons autant d’importance à la passion et à l’état d’esprit qu'à l'expérience. C'est pourquoi nous n'attendons pas de vous que vous possédiez toutes les compétences. Nous avons plutôt dressé une liste de celles qui, selon nous, vous aideront à réussir et à vous épanouir dans ce rôle :

Diplôme universitaire ou d'ingénieur en systèmes embarqués, télécommunications ou cybersécurité.
Expérience minimale de 3 ans. Une expérience dans le juridique, l'OT et idéalement dans le secteur ferroviaire est un plus.
Connaissance des concepts et techniques d'architecture des systèmes et réseaux, des systèmes d'exploitation et des langages de programmation associés.
Connaissance des principales techniques d'évaluation de la sécurité des systèmes.
Dynamisme, autonomie. Créativité et capacité à travailler dans un environnement complexe.
Connaissance des principales normes et réglementations de cybersécurité (telles que : ISO 2700X, IEC 62443, CRA, NIST, NIS) ou méthodes d'analyse des risques de cybersécurité est un plus.

Ce que vous apprécierez
Rejoignez-nous pour une nouvelle expérience de vie - le secteur ferroviaire est un secteur d’avenir, vous pouvez donc vous développer et acquérir de nouvelles compétences et expériences tout au long de votre carrière. Vous pourrez également :

Bénéficier de stabilité, de défis et d'une carrière à long terme sans routine quotidienne.
Perfectionner votre expertise cyber en traitant des sujets up-to-date dans ce domaine.
Travailler avec des équipes dynamiques et innovantes.
Collaborer avec des équipes transversales et des collègues qualifiés.
Contribuer à des projets innovants.
Utiliser notre environnement de travail axé sur la sécurité et l'innovation.
Orienter votre carrière dans la direction de votre choix à travers les fonctions et les pays.
Bénéficier de notre investissement dans votre développement, par le biais de programmes d’apprentissage primés.
Progresser vers des rôles de leadership en cybersécurité.
Bénéficier d'un système de rémunération équitable et dynamique qui reconnaît vos performances et votre potentiel, ainsi que d'une couverture sociale complète et compétitive (assurance-vie, assurance-maladie, pension).

Il n'est pas nécessaire d'être un passionné de trains pour s'épanouir chez nous. Nous vous garantissons que lorsque vous monterez dans l'un de nos trains avec vos amis ou votre famille, vous en serez fier. Si vous êtes prêt à relever le défi, nous aimerions vous connaître !

Alstom est une entreprise leader dans le secteur de la mobilité, qui résout les grands défis de la mobilité de demain. C'est pour cela que nous valorisons les personnes curieuses et innovantes qui sont passionnées par l’idée de travailler ensemble afin de réinventer la mobilité, de la rendre plus intelligente et plus durable. Jour après jour, nous construisons une culture agile, inclusive et responsable. Nos équipes, venant d’horizons différents, se voient offrir des opportunités d'apprendre, de se développer et de construire leur carrière en évoluant sur différentes fonctions et sites géographiques. Êtes-vous prêt à rejoindre une véritable communauté internationale pour une aventure stimulante et impactante ?

Equal Opportunities Statement:

Alstom garantit l'égalité des chances et s'engage en tant qu’employeur à créer un environnement de travail inclusif où tous sont encouragés à atteindre leur plein potentiel, et où les différences individuelles sont valorisées et respectées. Tous les candidats qualifiés sont considérés dans nos processus de recrutement sans tenir compte de l’origine, de la couleur de peau, de la religion, du sexe, de l'orientation sexuelle, de l'identité de genre, de l'âge, de la nationalité, de la nature du handicap ou de toute autre caractéristique protégée par la loi locale.

new_jobs.title: Strategy & Business Operations Manager, Wolt Drive
new_jobs.description:
About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we’re building the delivery of (almost) everything and you’ll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn’t always easy, but it’s definitely exciting. Here you’ll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You’ll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you’re a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

About The Role

Wolt is on a growth journey as part of the DoorDash family, together with Deliveroo. Drive
is our delivery-as-a-service business: we let merchants offer fast, reliable delivery in their own channels (their webshop, app or ordering system), powered by the Wolt and Deliveroo courier networks. We're now bringing Drive across Wolt and Deliveroo countries together into one EMEA business
, with one team and a clear ambition: grow fast and build a business that stands on its own feet.

A growing share of that scaling comes from outside restaurants: grocers, retailers, pharmacies and other eComm players who want on-demand and same-day delivery for their own customers. Their needs can be very different from restaurants: bigger baskets, scheduled and batched deliveries, larger and heavier items, longer distances and more complex integrations. This brings us to you, our next Manager, Strategy & Operations
for Grocery & Retail Drive.

You'll own this segment across EMEA, from strategy and planning to pricing, product requirements and performance. You'll work hand in hand with our regional commercial teams, who own the partner relationships, and with Product, Logistics, Finance and our Marketplace grocery & retail teams. You'll join the Drive EMEA Strategy & Operations team and report to the Director of Strategy & Operations, Drive EMEA.

What You'll Be Doing

Own the Grocery & Retail strategy and annual plan for Drive EMEA: where we play, which partners we go after, and the growth and profitability we commit to.
Set the commercial framework for the segment, including pricing guidelines, deal economics and investment cases for our largest partnerships, together with the regional commercial leads.

You will be responsible for all aspects of service transition, including: discovery & requirements gathering, implementing support models, conducting knowledge transfer & service readiness activities, managing go-live and warranty periods, and ultimately ensuring a smooth transition into steady-state operations.

Lead end-to-end service transition projects that onboard new customers and services into Managed Services support. Responsible for ensuring the service is transitioned smoothly to operational teams for steady-state delivery, creating a seamless end-user experience.

Lead & facilitate discovery workshops with the customer, internal operational teams, and 3rd party technology vendors.

Responsible for managing the handover from any incumbent (exiting service provider), protecting service continuity throughout the cutover.
Provide strong project leadership, driving collaboration with internal and external teams to ensure a robust operational support model is in place upon go-live.
Create and maintain project controls and governance, including: RAID, status reporting, project plan, forecasting, change requests, and budget management.

Demonstrable experience taking new services & customers through end-to-end onboarding, from contract signature to steady-state.
Solid experience in implementing operational support models & processes, service acceptance criteria, and runbooks/SOPs for newly transitioned services.
Experience in coordinating transition and handover from an incumbent (exiting service provider) including service-continuity planning.
Strong customer relationship building skills.
Skilled at identifying hidden/unstated client requirements.
Ability to lead and influence multi-disciplinary teams and stakeholders across the organization.
Highly organized, ability to manage constantly changing environment, project risks & requirements, and pressure.
Proven analytical and creative problem-solving abilities.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Experienced with best practice project management techniques and processes.

Certifications: ITIL and PMP qualifications are an asset.

As Senior Program Manager, you'll own the relationship and the delivery for d1g1t's most strategic clients. You'll be the senior leader who owns that process end-to-end: from scoping and planning through go-live and beyond. You'll sit inside the Program Management team and act as the primary bridge between d1g1t's technical teams and C-suite stakeholders at enterprise wealth firms. You will oversee multiple related projects, ensuring alignment with strategic goals, timely delivery and effective stakeholder communication. Twelve months in, your clients will have tighter implementations, cleaner escalation paths, and a clear sense that their partner understands their business.

What You'll Do

Own end-to-end program delivery for a portfolio of enterprise wealth management clients — from kickoff through go-live and into steady-state.
Serve as the primary escalation point for client issues, coordinating across internal teams (product, engineering, support) to resolve problems quickly and transparently.
Build and execute project plans, defining program scope, objectives, success metrics, accounting for competing timelines, resource constraints, and shifting client priorities — keeping stakeholders informed at every turn.
Drive strong delivery execution by anticipating, identifying, and mitigating program risks before they become incidents, and identifying dependencies; communicating clearly to executive-level stakeholders on both sides.
Leverage your financial domain knowledge to understand client problems at a business level — not just a ticket level — and drive outcomes that matter to wealth management operations.
Define and maintain delivery strategy, milestones, success criteria and key risks, aligned with the overall delivery roadmap.
Define and maintain detailed program plans, status reporting, facilitate regular program meetings, executive updates, and maintain rigorous oversight of the program/project plans, ensuring timelines, milestones and dependencies are consistently up to date.
Run structured feedback loops with clients to capture insights, drive continuous improvement, and feed learnings back into d1g1t's program methodology.
Partner with functional leaders internally to align on priorities, adjust work queues, and ensure client commitments are met without burning out the teams behind them.
Contribute continuously to the enhancement of the program management practices and governance frameworks.

What We're Looking For

7+ years in enterprise client relationship management or large-scale IT program management — ideally within a financial institution or fintech environment.
Deep familiarity with wealth or portfolio management as a domain: you understand the business problems your clients are trying to solve, not just the software they're implementing.
Active PMP certification and a strong working knowledge of the SDLC — you're as comfortable in a sprint review as you are in a client QBR.
A track record of delivering complex, multi-stakeholder projects on time, on budget, and within scope, even when priorities shift mid-stream.
Exceptional communication skills: you can explain a complex technical risk to a CFO without jargon, and explain a client's business constraint to an engineering team without losing the nuance.
Proficiency in modern project management tools (Asana, Notion, Slack) and the discipline to keep them current.
Emotional intelligence, with the ability to build trust and maintain effective relationships across diverse stakeholder groups. Exhibits self-awareness and composure under pressure, effectively navigating conflict, providing balanced, thoughtful resolution while maintaining team alignment.

Bonus Points

CFA designation or equivalent depth in investment management or financial planning concepts.
Experience scaling program management practices inside a fast-growing fintech or SaaS startup.
Demonstrated ability to shape process improvements that outlast any single client engagement.

What We Offer

Competitive compensation with performance bonus and comprehensive healthcare benefits. [recruiter: add comp band]
Hybrid-first work policy: primarily remote with 2 days/week in-office after. Ability to work abroad for up to 2 months per year (conditions apply).
Fitness & wellness credit, continuing education allowance, and an Employee & Family Assistance Program.
A genuinely collaborative culture at a fast-growing fintech where your instincts on process and client experience will actually get implemented.

Position Summary

The Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst III produces timely, accurate threat intelligence that supports a DHS agency's national cyber operations. The analyst fuses classified and unclassified intelligence, open-source, law enforcement, and partner reporting into products that help leaders and operators understand who is acting, how, and what is at risk.

The analyst works closely with watch floor, incident management, and hunt and response teams, adding threat context to active incidents and keeping leadership informed through regular and short-turn products.

Key Responsibilities

Threat Monitoring & Analysis

Continuously monitor intelligence, open-source, media, law enforcement, and partner reporting.
Analyze threat actors, campaigns, and tactics, techniques, and procedures, and map them to MITRE ATT&CK.
Assess relevance of threats to federal, state, local, tribal, territorial, and critical infrastructure partners.
Apply structured analytic techniques and clearly state confidence and sourcing.

Intelligence Products & Leadership Support

Contribute threat content to alerts, advisories, and partner communications.
Follow classification review and downgrade procedures so products can be shared at the right level.
Align products to the agency's existing critical information requirements and essential elements of information.

Incident & Operations Support

Give hunt and response teams leads drawn from intelligence reporting.
Support surge and crisis action activities during significant incidents.

Critical Infrastructure Context

Help analyze threats against critical infrastructure sectors, their dependencies, and potential consequences.
Contribute to operational and strategic reporting on critical infrastructure threats and vulnerabilities.

Tools & Data

Use and help improve threat intelligence platforms and sharing standards such as STIX and TAXII.
Review AI-generated summaries and enrichment for accuracy before release.

Minimum 5 years of experience in cyber threat intelligence analysis.
Working knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK, the Diamond Model, and the Cyber Kill Chain.
Experience with threat intelligence platforms and STIX/TAXII.
Experience writing intelligence products for senior government leaders.
Experience working with classified intelligence reporting.
Active Top Secret (TS) clearance.
Eligibility to obtain and maintain TS/SCI access.
Ability to work onsite at DHS Headquarters and other agency sites in the National Capital Region.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience at DHS, CISA, the Intelligence Community, DoD, or FBI cyber components.
Experience analyzing threats to critical infrastructure, including industrial control systems and operational technology.
Experience using Palantir or other enterprise analytics platforms for intelligence analysis.
Experience reviewing or validating AI-assisted analysis.GCTI, CTIA, or similar certifications.
Experience applying Intelligence Community analytic and sourcing standards (ICD 203 and ICD 206).
Experience managing intelligence requirements and requests for information, including tracking whether products met the need.
Familiarity with MITRE ATT&CK for ICS.
Ability to support nights, weekends, holidays, on-call, and work at a continuity site during emergencies.
Current DHS suitability (Entry on Duty) determination.
Experience handling information under the Traffic Light Protocol and controlled unclassified information (CUI) markings.

Dragos Global Threat Intelligence defends the infrastructure that powers civilization—from clean water and reliable power to food processing and oil & gas production. Every day, our team detects and defeats threats that could disrupt the operations millions of people depend on. We're seeking a Senior Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst to embed with an Australian customer team as a trusted, autonomous expert. You'll lead threat hunts, deliver tailored intelligence across multiple formats, and represent Dragos inside customer environments—making independent judgment calls that directly shape government strategy while collaborating across Dragos delivery teams to amplify intelligence impact. Our ideal candidate brings a proven track record delivering tailored threat intelligence in service organizations, hands-on threat hunting experience (both structured and exploratory), and working knowledge of industrial control systems (ICS).
